59769-bealby-a-holiday.title: A Holiday
59769-bealby-a-holiday.creator: Unknown
59769-bealby-a-holiday.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. the Shonts Velasquez—but that is now in America. And the Shonts Rubens, which is in the National Gallery. And the Shonts porcelain. And the Shonts past history; it was a refuge for the old faith; it had priest’s holes and secret passages. And how at last the Marquis had to let Shonts to the Laxtons—the Peptonized Milk and Baby Soother people—for a long term of years.

74022-little-sally-waters.title: Little Sally Waters
74022-little-sally-waters.creator: Ethel Calvert Phillips
74022-little-sally-waters.description: A book by Ethel Calvert Phillips. The truth is, Sally felt lonely. Not five minutes ago she had waved good-bye to Father and Mother as they started off for a day in the city. And as Sally remembered what a long, long day this was sure to be before she saw Father and Mother again, it really did seem as if Sally were going to cry.

arxiv-2103-07365.title: Speed of sound and baryon cumulants in heavy-ion collisions
arxiv-2103-07365.creator: Agnieszka Sorensen, Dmytro Oliinychenko, Volker Koch, Larry McLerran
arxiv-2103-07365.description: Abstract We present a method that may allow an estimate of the value of the speed of sound as well as its logarithmic derivative with respect to the baryon number density in matter created in heavy-ion collisions. To this end, we utilize well-known observables: cumulants of the baryon number distribution.

arxiv-2109-14561.title: Chiral criticality and the role of repulsive interactions in hot hadronic matter
arxiv-2109-14561.creator: Chihiro Sasaki
arxiv-2109-14561.description: Abstract We explore fluctuations of the net-baryon number density in hadronic matter at vanishing chemical potential. We discuss the interplay between chiral dynamics and repulsive interactions and their influence on the properties of these fluctuations near the chiral crossover in the parity doublet model.

arxiv-2305-02007.title: Detections of 21-cm absorption with a blind FAST survey at z ⩽ \leqslant 0.09
arxiv-2305-02007.creator: Wenkai Hu, Yougang Wang, Yichao Li, Yidong Xu, Wenxiu Yang, Guilaine Lagache, Ue-Li Pen, Zheng Zheng, Shuanghao Shu, Yinghui Zheng, Di Li, Tao-Chung Ching, Xuelei Chen
arxiv-2305-02007.description: Abstract We present the early science results from a blind search of the extragalactic Hi 21-cm absorption lines at z ⩽ 0.09 z\leqslant 0.09 with the drift-scan observation of the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST). We carried out the search using the data collected in 643.

arxiv-2311-00330.title: LATENT SPACE INFERENCE FOR SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS
arxiv-2311-00330.creator: Sayem Nazmuz Zaman (68943182), David Wang (99030033), Daniel Chen (43419712)
arxiv-2311-00330.description:
A 2023 arXiv research paper by Sayem Nazmuz Zaman (68943182), David Wang (99030033), Daniel Chen (43419712). EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

In order to understand the complexities of cellular biology, researchers are interested in two important metrics: the genetic expression information of cells and their spatial coordinates within a tissue sample. However, state-of-the art methods, namely single-cell RNA sequencing and image based spatial transcriptomics can only recover a subset of this information, either full genetic expression with loss of spatial information, or spatial information with loss of resolution in sequencing data.

arxiv-2404-13546.title: Electron and Muon ( g − 2 ) e , μ (g-2)_{e,\mu} Anomalous Magnetic Moment in U ​ ( 1 ) L e − L μ U(1)_{L_{e}-L_{\mu}} Symmetry Model
arxiv-2404-13546.creator: Rishu Verma a, Ankush a,b, B. C. Chauhan a
arxiv-2404-13546.description: Abstract The nature of neutrino (whether Majorana or Dirac) and the origin of neutrino masses are still some of the mysteries to be resolved. Also, the recent results on (g-2) e,μ measurements deviate from the Standard Model (SM) predictions and motivate us towards new physics beyond the SM.

arxiv-2407-02727.title: Long-lived magnetization in an atomic spin chain tuned to a diabolic point
arxiv-2407-02727.creator: R.J.G. Elbertse 1 , D. Borodin 2 , J. Oh 2,3 , T. Ahn 2,3 , J. Hwang 2,3 , J.C. Rietveld 1 , A.J. Heinrich 2,3 , F. Delgado 4 ∗ , S. Otte 1 ∗ , Y. Bae 2,3 ∗ † 1 Department of Quantum Nanoscience, Kavli Institute of Nanoscience, Delft University of Technology, Delft, The Netherlands 2 Center for Quan
arxiv-2407-02727.description: Abstract Scaling magnets down to where quantum size effects become prominent triggers quantum tunneling of magnetization (QTM), profoundly influencing magnetization dynamics. Measuring magnetization switching in an Fe atomic chain under a carefully tuned transverse magnetic field, we observe a non-monotonic variation of magnetization lifetimes around a level crossing, known as the diabolic point (DP).

arxiv-2502-06288.title: Enhancing Ground-to-Aerial Image Matching for Visual Misinformation Detection Using Semantic Segmentation
arxiv-2502-06288.creator: Emanuele Mule, Matteo Pannacci, Ali Ghasemi GoudarziFrancesco Pro, Lorenzo Papa, Luca Maiano, Irene AmeriniSapienza University of Rome {mule.1939852, pannacci.1948942, ghasemigoudarzi.2053156}@studenti.uniroma1.it{pro, papa, maiano, amerini}@diag.uniroma1.it
arxiv-2502-06288.description: Abstract The recent advancements in generative AI techniques, which have significantly increased the online dissemination of altered images and videos, have raised serious concerns about the credibility of digital media available on the Internet and distributed through information channels and social networks.

arxiv-2509-10165.title: Why Data Anonymization Has Not Taken Off
arxiv-2509-10165.creator: Matthew J. Schneider, James Bailie, Dawn Iacobucci
arxiv-2509-10165.description: Abstract Companies are looking to data anonymization research – including differential private and synthetic data methods – for simple and straightforward compliance solutions. But data anonymization has not taken off in practice because it is anything but simple to implement.

arxiv-2510-04522.title: Toward a Unified Geometry Understanding: Riemannian Diffusion Framework for Graph Generation and Prediction
arxiv-2510-04522.creator: Yisen Gao, Xingcheng Fu, Qingyun Sun, Jianxin Li, Xianxian Li
arxiv-2510-04522.description: Abstract Graph diffusion models have made significant progress in learning structured graph data and have demonstrated strong potential for predictive tasks. Existing approaches typically embed node, edge, and graph-level features into a unified latent space, modeling prediction tasks including classification and regression as a form of conditional generation.

arxiv-2510-07581.title: Expanding the Action Space of LLMs to Reason Beyond Language
arxiv-2510-07581.creator: Zhongqi Yue 1* Weishi Wang 2* Yundaichuan Zhan 3 Juncheng Li 3 Daniel Dahlmeier 2 Fredrik D. Johansson 1 1 Chalmers University of Technology and University of Gothenburg 2 SAP 3 Zhejiang University Project page: https://expa-rl.github.io/ *Equal contribution. zhongqi@chalmers.se, weishi.wang@sap.com
arxiv-2510-07581.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) are powerful reasoners in natural language, but their actions are typically confined to outputting vocabulary tokens. As a result, interactions with external environments—such as symbolic operators or simulators—must be expressed through text in predefined formats, parsed, and routed to external interfaces.

arxiv-2510-17841.title: Information Capacity of EEG: Theoretical and Computational Limits of Recoverable Neural Information
arxiv-2510-17841.creator: Ishir Rao
arxiv-2510-17841.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ishir Rao. Electroencephalography (EEG) is widely used to study human brain dynamics, yet its quantitative information capacity remains unclear. Here we combine information theory and synthetic forward modeling to estimate the mutual information between latent cortical sources and EEG recordings. Using Gaussian-channel theory [ 1 , 2 ] and empirical simulations, we find that scalp EEG conveys only tens of bits per sample about low-dimensional neural activity.

arxiv-2512-21811.title: A Story About Cohesion and Separation: Label-Free Metric for Log Parser Evaluation
arxiv-2512-21811.creator: Qiaolin Qin 1 , Jianchen Zhao 2 , Heng Li 1 , Weiyi Shang 2 , Ettore Merlo 1
arxiv-2512-21811.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Qiaolin Qin 1 , Jianchen Zhao 2 , Heng Li 1 , Weiyi Shang 2 , Ettore Merlo 1. Log parsing converts log messages into structured event templates, allowing for automated log analysis and reducing manual inspection effort. To select the most compatible parser for a specific system, multiple evaluation metrics are commonly used for performance comparisons.

plos-pone-0000577.creator: Tal Murthy, Andreas Rolfs, Yanhui Hu et al.
plos-pone-0000577.description: PLOS ONE research article. These clones must be full-length, sequence-verified and in a flexible format. The generatio

pmc-10488973.title: The Yin and the Yang of Hemostasis in End-Stage Liver Disease
pmc-10488973.creator: Fuat H Saner, Ecaterina Scarlatescu, Dieter Clemens Broering, Dmitri Bezinover, Pierluigi Toniutto
pmc-10488973.description: Patients with end-stage liver disease (ESLD) undergoing liver transplantation (LT) are prone to thromboses both while on the waiting list and in the perioperative period. This hypercoagulability is associated with significant endothelial dysfunction (ED) due to nitric oxide dysregulation. ED and increased thrombin generation are the main factors responsible for this hypercoagulability.

pmc-10566462.title: General acid-mediated aminolactone formation using unactivated alkenes†
pmc-10566462.creator: David Just, Carlos R. Gonçalves, Uroš Vezonik, Daniel Kaiser, Nuno Maulide
pmc-10566462.description: Spirocyclic butyrolactones and butenolides are widespread structural motifs in bioactive substances. Despite their prevalence, a simple method ensuring their direct preparation from exocyclic alkenes, ideally in a late-stage context, remains elusive. Herein, we report direct aminolactone formation using unactivated alkenes which addresses this gap, employing cheap and readily available reactants.

pmc-10600287.title: Bildgebung des postoperativen Beckenbodens
pmc-10600287.creator: Antonia M Pausch, Cornelia Betschart, Andreas M Hötker
pmc-10600287.description: Klinisches/methodisches ProblemDer Genitaldeszensus ist ein häufiges Krankheitsbild der Frau, wobei zur Therapie sowohl konservative als auch chirurgische Maßnahmen zur Verfügung stehen. Für die adäquate radiologische Diagnostik nach stattgehabter Deszensuschirurgie ist die Kenntnis der verschiedenen Operationsverfahren und des eingesetzten Fremdmaterials essenziell, um mögliche Komplikationen von normalen postoperativen Veränderungen zu unterscheiden.

pmc-10740868.title: The Impact of UFP-512 in Mice with Osteoarthritis Pain: The Role of Hydrogen Sulfide
pmc-10740868.creator: Gerard Batallé, Xue Bai, Gianfranco Balboni, Olga Pol, Reto Asmis
pmc-10740868.description: The pain-relieving properties of opioids in inflammatory and neuropathic pain are heightened by hydrogen sulfide (H2S). However, whether allodynia and functional and/or emotional impairments related to osteoarthritis (OA) could be reduced by activating δ-opioid receptors (DOR) and the plausible influence of H2S on these actions has not been completely established.

pmc-10775042.title: Association of dementia with clinical and financial outcomes following lobectomy for lung cancer
pmc-10775042.creator: Konmal Ali, Sara Sakowitz, Nikhil L Chervu, Arjun Verma, Syed Shahyan Bakhtiyar, Joanna Curry, Nam Yong Cho, Peyman Benharash
pmc-10775042.description: ObjectiveThe number of adults with dementia is rising worldwide. Although dementia has been linked with inferior outcomes following various operations, this phenomenon has not been fully elucidated among patients undergoing elective lung resection. Using a national cohort, we evaluated the association of dementia with clinical and financial outcomes following lobectomy for cancer.

pmc-11662651.title: Glucose binds and activates NSUN2 to promote translation and epidermal differentiation
pmc-11662651.creator: Weili Miao, Douglas F Porter, Ya Li, Lindsey M Meservey, Yen-Yu Yang, Chengjie Ma, Ian D Ferguson, Vivian B Tien, Timothy M Jack, Luca Ducoli, Vanessa Lopez-Pajares, Shiying Tao, Paul B Savage, Yinsheng Wang, Paul A Khavari
pmc-11662651.description: Elevations in intracellular glucose concentrations are essential for epithelial cell differentiation by mechanisms that are not fully understood. Glucose has recently been found to directly bind several proteins to alter their functions to enhance differentiation. Among the newly identified glucose-binding proteins is NSUN2, an RNA-binding protein that we identified as indispensable for epidermal differentiation.

pmc-11874416.title: Emerging technology solutions to support national emergency workforce capacity-building initiatives: lessons from Ugandan policy and practice
pmc-11874416.creator: Emily McMullen, Solomon Kamurari, Richard Price, Moses Mulimira, Jonathan James, Andrew Fryer, Daudi Jjingo
pmc-11874416.description: Trauma and emergency care is a national priority in Uganda due to the high burden of injury, impacting a primarily young and rural population. With a significant gap in qualified emergency medicine professionals, a need exists to rapidly upskill the current health workforce and to strengthen access to learning for non-specialist emergency care providers nationally.

pmc-13198873.title: Hypervirulent and Drug-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae: Clinical Challenges and Alternative Treatment Strategies
pmc-13198873.creator: Sulaiman Bani Abdel-Rahman, Hala Altarawneh, Hassan Ahmad Hasan Alfreahat, Khulud A Alhazmi, Ohood S Alharbi, Malaz Gazzaz, Turki M Alharthi, Loui A Ismaeel, Waiel S Halabi, Asim T Sharif, Bayan Redwan, Khalil K Alkuwaity, Wafaa Alhazmi, Bandar Hasan Saleh, Mona A Alqarni, Abdulaziz Alsaedi, Nabeel
pmc-13198873.description: Klebsiella pneumoniae is a major opportunistic pathogen responsible for a wide range of hospital- and community-acquired infections, including respiratory tract infections, urinary tract infections, meningitis, and liver abscesses. Among its emerging forms, hypervirulent K. pneumoniae (hvKp) has gained global attention due to its heightened virulence and ability to cause severe infections in healthy individuals. hvKp differs from classical K.

pmc-13208330.title: Admission Electrolyte Abnormalities and Clinical Outcomes in Hospitalized COVID-19 Patients
pmc-13208330.creator: Emine Önder, Aysun Ekinci, Fırat Aşır, Cigdem Mermutluoglu, Erdal Ozbek, Pakize Gamze Erten Bucaktepe, Ismail Yildiz
pmc-13208330.description: Background and Objectives: Electrolyte abnormalities are frequently observed in hospitalized patients with acute infections and may reflect underlying disease severity. This study aimed to investigate the association between baseline electrolyte disturbances and clinical outcomes in patients with COVID-19, with a particular focus on albumin-corrected calcium levels. Materials and Methods: This retrospective study included 348 hospitalized patients with COVID-19.

pmc-13396503.title: Energy-efficient, real-time detection of railway fastening systems from drone-based imagery using spiking neural networks
pmc-13396503.creator: Sakdirat Kaewunruen, Zibo Chen, Aryadhatu Dhaniswara, Zahid Hamarat
pmc-13396503.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Rail fastener defects threaten track integrity and operational safety, making reliable automated inspection essential. This study develops an energy-efficient real-time railway fastener detection framework for UAV-based monitoring by integrating Spiking Neural Networks (SNN) into a modified Spiking-YOLOv8 architecture. Unlike conventional CNNs, the event-driven SNN processes only informative visual changes, reducing redundant computation, and achieving a better accuracy–energy balance for on-board inspection.

pmc-13411859.title: When is elimination of an infectious disease cost-effective? An analytical framework to guide elimination priorities
pmc-13411859.creator: Sayara Ahmed, Tara D. Mangal, Timothy B. Hallett, Hugo C. Turner
pmc-13411859.description: BackgroundElimination targets for infectious diseases are increasingly common in global health, yet the economic rationale for pursuing elimination is often assumed rather than rigorously assessed. Existing evaluations frequently emphasise future cost savings or broader economic benefits while overlooking health opportunity costs—the health that could have been gained had resources been allocated elsewhere.
